title: EU backs QIA quantum network prototype with $53M grant
key_facts: The Quantum Internet Alliance (QIA) received about $53 million from the European Commission for a programmable quantum network prototype.
The 42-month programme aims to link two metropolitan-scale quantum networks over long-distance fibre using quantum repeaters.
QIA is a European consortium of universities, research institutes and companies; members include QuTech, Delft Networks, TIM, Telefonica and AMS-IX.
The first phase ran from October 2022 to March 2026; this second grant agreement integrates the parts into a full system.
The prototype is meant to run quantum network applications beyond quantum key distribution (encryption keys).
Delft Networks and Eurofiber have a dark-fibre loop between Delft and Rotterdam for testing entanglement distribution.
quote_evidence: Our mission in this next phase is to integrate these components into a full stack quantum internet prototype, QIA Director Stephanie Wehner explained.
The 42-month program aims to connect two metropolitan quantum networks over long-distance fiber using quantum repeaters.
The project forms part of QIA's seven-year program to connect distant cities, launched under a partnership agreement with the European Commission in 2022.
why_it_matters_hint: Europe is funding the next step towards a working quantum internet linking cities.
notes: Dollar figure as given by SDxCentral; its URL slug says 475m, so the grant may be about 47.5 million euros. Original QIA or European Commission announcement not read.
